correctness.rationale: For a>1 the torus parametrization r=sqrt(s+cos(theta)), z=sin(theta) is regular. Both z and r are conserved; angular dynamics is dphi/dt=-(R sqrt(s+u)cos(phi)+d sin(theta)), and a simple latitude is a nonstationary cycle iff F_eta(u)=eta^2(1-u^2)-s-u>0. Minimizing (s+u)/(1-u^2) gives unique u*=-s+sqrt(s^2-1), eta*^2=(s+sqrt(s^2-1))/2; strict above-threshold concavity produces two ±z annuli. Exact period is 2pi/(R sqrt(F)). With h half root width, F=eta^2 h^2(1-xi^2), and the true torus area factor J(u)=sqrt((s+u)u^2+(1-u^2)/4). The two-hemisphere area integrals yield A/sqrt(delta)->8pi J*/eta* and finite weighted W->8pi^3 J*/(R eta* v*). Uniform smooth-factor convergence under the integrable inverse square-root density proves total-variation arcsine latitude and exact independent half signs. Independently checked rational witness s=4,eta^2=4: roots -1/4 and 0, F at midpoint 1/16, period 8pi. Numeric checks in inspected CHECK.py are corroboration only, not the source of universal proof.
